source.title: Feynman integrals as generalized functions on path space: things done and open problems

accepted.question_text: Within the white-noise generalized-function approach to Feynman path integrals, can the construction of non-perturbative Feynman integrals be extended by weakening the requirement that the expression inside the relevant expectation be integrable, while still yielding a valid T-transform and hence a well-defined generalized white-noise functional?

For quantum fields phi, vacuum vector Omega, time-ordering operator T, and a test function f, is the time-ordered vacuum expectation value <Omega, T exp(i phi(f)) Omega> holomorphic as a function of f after continuation from Schwinger functions to the corresponding time-ordered Minkowski functions?

evidence.quote: Time ordered expectation values of quantum fields

needs_review.question_text_raw: A new look at the change of variables in the Feynman integral.

trace.notes: Normalized the single input URL as a zbMATH document locator. A local shell fetch of https://zbmath.org/5605356 failed with DNS error curl code 6, so zbMATH was treated as a resolver rather than the readable technical source.

Recovered the exact work title from local resolver data and web-indexed bibliographic records: Feynman integrals as generalized functions on path space: things done and open problems. Exact-title recovery found a full proceedings PDF at the Pelster/FU Berlin site. The PDF's table of contents and article heading confirmed the same title and author L. Streit, with the article on pages 78-85.

Mapped the article structure: 1. Introduction: The Feynman Integral, pages 78-79; 2. How to Recognize a Generalized Function When You See One, page 80; 3. Construction, pages 80-81; 4. Classes of Admissible Interactions, pages 81-82; 5. Boundary Value Problems, pages 82-83; 6. Beyond Perturbation Theory, page 83; 7. A Glimpse at (E)QFT, page 84; 8. Things to be Done, page 84. Key terms include white-noise measure, Hida distribution, Kondratiev distribution, T-transform, Feynman integrand, Schrodinger equation, vacuum density, Schwinger functions, and time-ordered functions.

The introductory question asking whether a formal Feynman expression is a continuous map from test functions is presented as motivation and then addressed by the framework, so it was not extracted as an open-problem candidate.

Extracted an implicit open direction about non-perturbative Feynman integrals from the discussion of integrability in the Doss complex-scaling approach and the later explicit Things to be Done bullet.

Extracted the open question about holomorphy of time-ordered vacuum expectations after the source states that convergence after continuation from Schwinger functions is unknown except for free fields.

Extracted all three bullets from Things to be Done. The first two have enough same-source context for a self-contained rewrite; the third is too terse to determine the intended change-of-variables problem without adding unsupported detail.

Rewrote the bullet about relaxing integrability using the Section 6 context: non-perturbative Feynman integrals are discussed through complex scaling and the T-transform characterization, where integrability is identified as the condition to relax.

Expanded the source's compact holomorphy question by inlining the entities named in the surrounding paragraph: quantum fields, vacuum vector, time ordering, test function f, Schwinger functions, and time-ordered Minkowski functions.

Could not expand the change-of-variables bullet into a self-contained technical question because the source gives no same-source definition of what change of variables, admissible transformation class, or failure mode is intended.
